This case is arose out of Crime No.0157/2018 of Upparapete Police Station registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC and 39, 76 Chit Fund Act, 1982 based on the gist of facts stated in the FIR which has set this criminal case in motion against the accused.

2. The case of the prosecution is that accused lives in leased out house No.6/2, Tulasi thota Road,
Upparapete, Bengaluru obtained from CW12, when accused was residing in Akkipete and certain places she use to collect chit amount every month without having - 3-- CC-4934/2019 any license to run the chit business since 2015, she failed to pay the chit amount of Rs.10,75,000/- in favour of CW.1 and 2, Rs.3,59,660/- in favour of CW3, Rs.2,54,660/- in favour of CW4, Rs.3,60,400/- in favour of CW5, Rs.3,38,000/- in favour of CW6, Rs.3,30,000/- in favour of CW7, Rs.4,00,000/- in favour of CW8, Rs.7,63,025/- in favour of CW9, Rs.13,60,000/- in favour of CW10, Rs.2,00,000/- in favour of CW11 on the expiry of the term of the chit transaction,
3.

The Upparapete Police had booked the case against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC and 39, 76 Chit Fund Act, 1982 based on the written complaint of Sri.
Kum. Asha.M.
The Investigating Officer registered the FIR, prepared the spot and seizure panchanama, recorded the statement of witnesses and collected the documents.
Having material in the investigation, Investigating Officer filed charge sheet against the accused for the offences alleged.
4. Upon receipt of the court summons, the accused has entered appearance before the court.
The relevant copies have been furnished under Section 207 of Cr. P.C. to the accused.
The - 4-- CC-4934/2019 charge for the offences under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC and 39, 76 Chit Fund Act, 1982 framed, explained and read over to the accused before the court.
Upon which accused has pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried before the court.
5. In the instant case, the prosecution examined CW1 as PW1, CW2 as PW2, CW8 as PW3, CW15 as PW4, CW10 as PW5, CW9 as PW6, CW13 as PW7, CW14 as PW8, CW16 as PW9 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P20.
Despite issuing summons, warrants and proclamation warrants, presence of CW3 to CW7 and CW12 were not secured.
CW11 reported to be dead.
Thereby, CW3 to CW7 and CW12 were dropped from the charge sheet.
Evidence on prosecution side closed.

3  Point No.1 to 3:- IN THE NEGATIVE  Point No.4:- As per final order for the following:-
 REASONS 10. Point No.1 to 3:-
All these points require common discussion.
As the findings to be given on particular point has the direct bearing on other points.
Therefore, so as to avoid the repetition of discussion and conclusion.
I have taken all these points for consideration at one stretch.
11. According to the prosecution version CW1 to 11 are the victims of the crime.
CW1 lodged police complaint against the accused.
CW.1 has been cited as complainant witness in the charge sheet.
CW2 to 11 have been cited as witnesses in the charge sheet.
CW1 and 2 are none other than mother and daughter.

CW1 and 2 deposed that financial dispute took place between accused and themselves were settled, they said that nothing more than the financial transaction took place among them, they have not given any statement before the police.
These - 7-- CC-4934/2019 two witnesses have been declared hostile witnesses.
During the course of cross-examination by the Senior Public Prosecutor, they have not given any evidence against the accused.
Therefore, evidence of these two witnesses not avail to the prosecution.

12. CW8-Saraswathi has been examined as PW3, CW10-Girija has been examined as PW.5,
CW9-Gayathri has been examined as PW6.
CW11 reported to be dead.
CW3 to 7 who stated to be victims of the crime did not step into the witness box in response to the summons, warrants and proclamation warrants issued against them to the court.
This being the position, the evidences of the Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri must be appreciated to understand offence alleged against the accused is proved or not by the prosecution.
13. Smt.Saraswathi deposed that she became a subscriber of two chit amounting to Rs.2 Lakhs with accused for the past 10 years, she use to pay a sum of Rs.10,000/- every month per chit.
accused executed a bond agreeing to repay an amount of Rs.4 Lakhs in her favour.
Bond executed in favour of Smt. Saraswathi by the accused marked at Ex.P12 in the evidence.

. Smt. Girija deposed that she became a subscriber of two chit amounting to Rs.1,50,000/- and daughter Kavitha became a subscriber of one chit amounting to Rs.2,50,000/- with the accused for the past 10 years, they use to pay a sum of Rs.34,000/- every month till 2017, accused executed a bond agreeing to repay an amount of Rs.8,60,000/- in her favour and Rs.5 Lakhs in favour of her daughter.
Bond executed in favour of Smt. Girija by the accused marked at Ex.P4 and 5 in the evidence.

4 15.

Smt.Gayathri deposed that mother and herself became subscribers of two chit amounting to Rs.2,50,000/- and Rs.50,000/- with the accused since 2015, they use to pay a sum of Rs.18,000/-
every month till 2017, accused executed a bond agreeing to repay an amount of Rs.7,63,050/- in her favour.
Bond executed in favour of Smt.Gayathri by the accused marked at Ex.P6 in the evidence.
16. All the three witnesses deposed that they often demanded for return the chit amount with the accused, accused failed to pay the amount.
During the cross-examination of the above three witnesses the accused had raised so many defenses.

The defenses raised by the accused are as follows: 1) there are no any agreement - 9-- CC-4934/2019 regarding chit transaction or document regarding the payment of the chit amount to the accused, there are no nexus between the accused and the books and those books fabricated for the purpose of the case 2) how many persons were the subscribers of the chit and membership number of the subscribers are not known to the witnesses, 3) the date, month, year and venue of the commencement of the chit and ending of the chit are not known to the witnesses, 4)
bonds do not contain the signatures of the witnesses and the signatures of the accused on bonds and bonds are concocted for the purpose of case, 5) the accused was not doing any chit transaction and the witnesses never had chit transaction with the accused and 6) a false case has been foisted against the accused.

That apart, the defense able to extract from the mouth of these witnesses that according to the Government rules a person who possess license can only run the chit transaction and they are under obligation to know had the accused obtained license to run the chit transaction.
17. Accused strongly contends that she was not doing any chit transaction, she never had chit transaction with Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri, there are no nexus between the accused and the -
 - 10 CC-4934/2019 books, those books fabricated for the purpose of the case.
Four chit books marked as Ex.P15 to 18 and two Ledger Books marked as Ex.P19 and Ex.P20.
Investigating Officer deposed that 4 Chit Books and 2 Ledger Books recovered in the presence of panchas at the house of accused vide seizure mahazar dated 02.08.2018.
According to the defense version the accused was not present at the time of recovery of the chit books and ledger books and at that relevant point of time she was resided in Marathahalli.
Aforesaid seizure panchanama does not contain signature of the accused.
CW13-PW7 and CW14-PW8 Pancha witnesses of seizure mahazar testified that dairy and note books were not recovered in their presence by the police, they signed seizure mahazar at the police station.
Thereby, recovery of the chit books and ledger books at the instance of accused has not been proved through the independent pancha witnesses evidence.
Ex.P15 to Ex.P18 small books do not contain signatures of the Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri.
Ex.P.19 and Ex.P20 Ledger Books do not clearly demonstrate the payment of chit amount as told by Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri in their depositions.
There are no reference of how much amount Asha.

M vs Gowramma on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100771216/
5 owe by the accused to Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri.

Signatures of Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri can be -
- 11 CC-4934/2019 ascertained here and there in the Ledger Books.
The accused urges that those books fabricated for the purpose of the case.
That being so, opinion of the handwriting expert regarding handwriting and signatures of the Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri are very crucial.
The Investigating Officer did not make any attempt to obtain handwriting expert opinion so as to prove authenticity of the Ex.P15 to Ex.P20.

In the absence of such proof, court cannot hold that chit transaction took place between the accused and Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri relying upon Ex.P15 to Ex.P20.
18.
Accused do contend that bonds do not contain the signatures of the attesting witnesses and bonds are concocted for the purpose of case.
She denies signature of her in the bond.
Original bonds have been produced for the inspection of the court as Ex.P4 to Ex.P6 and Ex.P12.
Therefore, the initial burden is on the prosecution to establish that signatures are in deed that of accused in the Ex.P4 to Ex,P6 and Ex.P12.
Under Section 2(5) of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 bond shall be attested by witness when a person obliges himself to pay money to another.
Under Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act, atleast one attesting witness must be called to prove its execution.

In the instant case,
prosecution is not -
- 12 CC-4934/2019 able to establish that chit transaction took place between the accused and Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri.
Denial of the signature and execution of the bonds is specific on the part of the accused.
No one shown as attesting witness in the bonds.
Besides, Investigating Officer has not secured the handwriting expert opinion regarding the genuinety or otherwise of the signatures of the accused said to be found on the bonds.
Position stood thus, court cannot hold that bonds were executed towards payment of chit amount by the accused.
19. Prosecution is not able to prove that chit transaction took place between the accused and Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri and bonds were executed towards payment of chit amount by the accused.

The defense able to cull out from the testimony of the Saraswathi, Girija and Gayathri that how many persons were the subscribers of the chit, membership number of the subscribers, date,
month, year and venue of the commencement of the chit and ending of the chit are not known.
Thereby, there are no any kind of evidence to hold that accused was doing unauthorized chit business as alleged by the prosecution.

-
- 13 CC-4934/2019 Asha. M vs Gowramma

on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100771216/
6 20.

The prosecution fails to establish that CW1 to CW11 had entrusted amount towards the chit transaction to the accused and then accused converted the chit amount for her own benefit,
prosecution is also failed to establish that accused dishonestly induced the CW1 to CW11 to pay the chit amount.
Further, prosecution failed to prove that accused was running unregistered chit transaction or carrying on chit business without sanction from the Government.
In view of the above, the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC and 39, 76 Chit Fund Act, 1982 not made out.
Accordingly, accused is entitled for acquittal of the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC and 39, 76 Chit Fund Act, 1982.
Hence, I record findings on Point No.1 to 3 in the NEGATIVE.

21. Point No.4:- For the reasons discussed in the Point No.1 to 3, I pass the following:
ORDER
In exercise of power conferred under Section 248(1) of Cr. P.C. accused found not guilty of the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC and 39, 76 Chit Fund Act, 1982.

-
- 14 CC-4934/2019 The bail bond and surety bond of the accused is extended for a period of 6 months in compliance of Section 437(A) of Cr. P.C.
